key_insight: A solver-guided LLM can learn to choose the best MIP formulation for each multi-warehouse inventory allocation instance, rather than relying on one fixed formulation.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, higher-quality inventory decisions in real retail systems by matching each instance to the formulation most likely to optimize allocation performance.
method: Build a candidate library of OR experts, each encoding a different allocation priority as a MIP formulation.
Create balanced supervised fine-tuning data for schema learning, then turn solver-evaluated quality gaps into margin-weighted IPO preferences.
Use GRPO with per-instance expert-score rewards to train the selector to pick the best formulation.
evidence_signal: On JD.com inventory allocation instances, GRPO improved Hit Ratio@1 from 21.45% to 50.42% and Hit Ratio@2 from 70.47% to 82.31%, while reducing the gap to the ex-post oracle to 4.85 percentage points.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality solver feedback and a curated expert library, so performance may degrade if the candidate formulations or historical labels do not cover new instance regimes.
paper_title: Large Language Model for Operations Research Formulation Selection in Multi-Warehouse Inventory Allocation
